A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts and supplementary sections, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original shadow-detection comparisons, ablations, light-estimation experiments, runtime measurements and a shadow-removal user study.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark tables, supplementary light-estimation results and 259-vote user study.

M1.justification: The SILT/PVT detector, ConvNeXt-S light estimator, normal-light partial mask, iterative feedback and losses remain unchanged. Added explanations about the coarse prior and learning from imperfect geometry cues describe the existing procedure; they do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,458-image dataset assembled from WSRD, SOBA and CUHK, plus qualitative evaluation on SRD, SBU-TimeLapse and ViSha. Shadow-removal and light-estimation task coverage is also retained.

E2.justification: Main Table 2 retains BDRAR, DSD, FSDNet, MTMT, FDRNet, SDCM and SILT, with the same four fine-tuned variants. Supplementary Table 1 also retains the fine-tuned BDRAR+Normal and SILT+Normal comparisons.

E3.justification: Supplementary Section 3.3 changes the stated normal-map coordinate convention: positive z points toward the camera in v2 but inward in v3. This revises a reported preprocessing setting, without establishing regenerated inputs or rerun experiments. Splits, metrics, training budgets and user-study procedures otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The normal-input, iteration-count and loss ablations are retained, as are the light-refinement analysis, foreground-only examples, cross-dataset demonstrations and normal-estimation failure example. No new robustness or supplementary analytical evidence is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point estimates and the same user-study vote aggregation. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, training seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Main Table 2 corrects pretrained BDRAR's attached F1 from 53.32 to 52.32 and the proposed method's attached BER from 12.93 to 12.92. Both revised values already appeared in v2's supplementary Table 1. These reconcile reporting inconsistencies rather than demonstrate new performance gains; other results are retained.

T1.justification: Supplementary Section 3.3 corrects the definition of the positive normal-map z-axis from toward the camera to inward, aligning its stated direction with the light-coordinate frame. This is a limited geometric-definition correction; Equations (1)-(9) and the single-directional-light assumption remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract now explicitly qualifies the framework claim with a dominant directional-light setting, and the introduction describes geometric inference as partial. This makes an existing restriction more explicit in the headline claims. The joint-detection, iterative-refinement, dataset and at-least-33% attached-BER contributions remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds the explanation that training with estimated partial maps teaches use of imperfect geometry cues. It recasts reduced annotation effort as a potential benefit, explicitly characterizes supplementary generalization evidence as qualitative, and describes three iterations as a performance-efficiency tradeoff. The principal limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The normal-coordinate correction in Supplementary Section 3.3 revises a consequential implementation specification. Architecture details, hyperparameters, GPU requirements, inference times, annotation procedures and the project-page link otherwise remain unchanged; no new resource availability is reported.

R1.justification: v3 adds mli-NeRF, replaces the NTIRE 2023 challenge-report reference with the WSRD benchmark paper, and removes three peripheral citations concerning UAV, satellite and RGB/HSV shadow applications. Central research positioning remains stable. Most other bibliography changes concern formatting or publication metadata.

P1.justification: v3 makes local prose and terminology refinements throughout, expands the introductory explanation, adds acknowledgements and supplementary title/author information, and standardizes the bibliography. The section sequence and overall narrative are retained.

P2.justification: Existing figures and tables are retained, with caption and label refinements such as Joint to Unified and a shortened ground-truth annotation label. Figure 4, Table 3 and Figure 9 move through page reflow, and the supplement gains a separate title block. No new scientific display is added.

improvement.justification: v3 improves reporting consistency by reconciling two Table 2 values with the existing appendix and aligning the stated normal-axis convention with the light-coordinate frame. More explicit lighting qualifications and more cautious interpretations better match the retained evidence. These are useful, limited improvements in clarity and reliability; the underlying method and empirical support remain essentially unchanged.
